---
title: "Before analysis"
---

**Pause point:** Before running the analysis that will support an interpretable result or research claim.

**Prevents:** Analysing the wrong data, changing decisions invisibly, using a method that cannot answer the question, or losing the provenance of results.

**Use:** Do-confirm.

## Critical checks

- [ ] The research question, outcome or interpretive purpose is explicit enough to guide the analysis.
- [ ] The authorised input data are identified, versioned and separated from derived data and outputs.
- [ ] Inclusion, exclusion, cleaning, transformation, coding and missing-data decisions are recorded.
- [ ] The method fits the design, data and intended inference, and its important assumptions can be examined.
- [ ] Planned, amended, sensitivity and exploratory analyses are distinguished rather than retrospectively presented as one plan.
- [ ] Code, software versions, packages, settings and dependencies are recorded well enough to recover the analysis.
- [ ] A second check is planned for critical inputs, calculations, code or interpretations.
- [ ] Confidential or identifiable data will not be exposed through working files, logs, outputs or sharing.
- [ ] Deviations from the approved protocol or analysis plan have been authorised and recorded where required.
- [ ] Outputs have a stable location and an auditable link to the inputs and code that produced them.

## Stop condition

Pause if the input dataset is unstable, exclusions cannot be explained, or the method cannot be linked defensibly to the question and design.

## Evidence to retain

Keep the frozen input reference, analysis plan, data decisions, scripts or commands, environment record, quality checks, deviations and final output manifest.

::: {.callout-warning title="Check locally"}
Specialist methods, sensitive data and regulated analyses may require formal review, validation or controlled computing environments.
:::
